newsitem.title: USA: US distillate output in Oct near 20-year high - API.
newsitem.headline: US distillate output in Oct near 20-year high - API.

text.p: U.S. distillate production in October leaped to 3.65 million barrels per day, just below the record set nearly 20 years ago, American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
October output of distillates -- heating oil and diesel -- was 15 percent higher than a year ago and helped build stocks which were far below average for this time of year.
At the same time, distillate demand, measured in deliveries, surged 13.6 percent from a year ago to 3.53 million bpd, API said in its monthly statistical report.
Total U.S. demand for petroleum products climbed 5.2 percent from October last year to 18.57 million bpd.
Jet kerosine deliveries hit a record high of 1.71 million bpd, up 12.5 percent from a year ago with the help of rapid growth in commercial airline travel, API said.
Gasoline deliveries reached 7.86 million bpd, up 1 percent from October 1995.

But gasoline stocks dipped to a historic low of 190 million barrels in October, nearly 14 million barrels off a year ago. The low reflected "a trend toward lower stock levels that has persisted since the beginning of 1994," API said.
Deliveries of residual fuel in October fell 1.6 percent from a year ago to 812,000 bpd, although API said underlying demand for fuel oil was about the same as last October.

U.S. crude production, including condensates, averaged 6.48 million bpd in October, up 0.9 percent from a year ago. A 120,000 bpd increase in the lower 48 states helped offset a 60,000 bpd drop in Alaskan production.
Total petroleum imports soared 14.4 percent from last October to 9.8 million bpd, with 7.77 million bpd of crude.
Distillate imports of 222,000 bpd were up 60,000 bpd from October 1995.
